title: Best tips for running a profitable lightning node?

answer.summary: Practical, tested advice for running a profitable Lightning Network node.
points: Pick your strategy first: routing fees, channel leasing (e.g. liquidity marketplaces), or holding inbound liquidity for a service. Routing alone rarely pays back capital costs on small nodes.
Channel selection matters more than node size. Open channels to well-connected, honest peers (Amboss, 1ML reputation, LNBig, Bitrefill) with good uptime and balanced two-way flow.
Set fees with data, not guesses. Start at ~0.1% base / 1 ppm and adjust based on your forwarding statistics over 1-2 weeks. Watch forward vs. local fail rates.
Maintain balanced liquidity: use circular rebalancing through cheap peers when a channel is one-sided, and consider swaps (Loop) when on-chain costs are low.
Watch your cost basis: on-chain fees at open/close, VPS cost, and time. A node under ~0.1 BTC routed volume per month usually operates at a loss on routing fees alone.
Run reliable software (Core Lightning or LND on latest stable), keep 99%+ uptime, enable watchtowers, and keep a hot wallet only as large as you can afford to lose.
Track profitability per channel with tools like lnmetrics, RTL, or LNMonitor dashboards; close chronically unprofitable channels.
Consider paid services that leverage your node: channel leasing (Lightning Pool style), serving as an LSP for wallet apps, or routing for merchants - these often beat raw routing fees.
Tax and regulatory note: fee income is generally taxable income in most jurisdictions; keep records from day one.
